newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - May 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - May 12.

text.p: THE DOMINION

Reluctant GPs could miss out on subsidy: Associate Health Minister Neil Kirton has advised general practitioners balking at providing free care for children under six that a higher government subsidy might be withheld from those who do not sign up to the policy. Page 1.

PM raises nave hopes on extra frigates: The navy's hopes of getting a third and possibly fourth new frigate were raised after Prime Minister Jim Bolger told guests at the launch of new frigate Te Mana that the government was committed to a blue water navy. Page 1.

Peters fuels talk of Shipley challenge: Deputy Prime Minister Winston Peters has fuelled mounting speculation State Services Minister Jenny Shipley is positioning herself to replace Prime Minister Jim Bolger. Page 1.

Nats keep open mind on future partner: National had no intention of going into the next with NZ First, or any other party, as a pre-arranged coalition partner, party president Geoff Thompson said at the weekend. Page 2.
ATN manager accused of sexual misconduct: A senior Aotearoa Television Network manager was accused of sexual misconduct, an audit by Maori broadcasting agency Te Mangai Paho found. Page 2.

Powers over ATN funder refused, says Williamson: Communications Minister Maurice Williamson has said he was not given the powers he wanted over Maori broadcasting funding agency Te Mangai Paho because it would have been seen as "insulting and patronising" to Maoris. Page 3.

Anderton raises questions about commissioner fees: Treaty of Waitangi fisheries commissioners came under further scrutiny on Sunday, with Alliance leader Jim Anderton saying he had found an unexplained $644,000 discrepancy in their 1994 fees. Page 12.

McCully calls rent rise reports misleading: Comments by opposition housing spokesman Graham Kelly last week about Housing NZ rent increases were grossly misleading and totally unbalanced, Housing Minister Murray McCully said. Page 12.
Telecom's heyday over say analysts: Telecom Corp's days of posting ever-burgeoning profits may be over, analysts say. Page 13.

Wellington job ads rise slightly: Job advertisements in Wellington rose slightly in April, the first rise for many months, but the number of advertisements is still well below levels of a year ago, the latest ANZ Bank survey says. Page 13.

Analysts expect Carter Holt profit to drop by 45pc: Forest products giant Carter Holt Harvey is expected to report a decline of about 45 percent in full-year net profit on Tuesday, reflecting a slump in prices for pulp, paper, lumber and logs. Page 13.
CIL believes Montana can contribute more: Investment company Corporate Investments expects annual net profit from its main investment, Montana Wines, to be higher than last year. Page 13.

Bank says the unskilled should not fear Asia: Unskilled workers in rich industraliased countries had more to fear from technological advances than increased trade with the Asian region, the Asian Development Bank said on Sunday. Page 15.

Muck makes more money for Waste Management: Company chairman Alton Jamieson told the annual meeting last week that the March-quarter tax-paid profit was up 19 percent on the March 1996 quarter. Page 15.

Plan set up to reverse Otago business slide: A strategic plan to arrest the erosion of Otago's economic base has been made public by a Dunedin business group that aims to encourage a positive attitude in the region. Page 15.
Knitting yarns merger cleared: The Commerce Commission has cleared the merger of the Australian and New Zealand knitting yarns and crafts businesses of Alliance Textiles and Coats Patons. Page 15.
THE NEW ZEALAND HERALD

Lines linked to new health fears: New Zealand researchers have linked high-tension power lines -- already associated with higher tales of leukaemia among children -- to asthma and depression in adults.
Payouts settle row at Viaduct: A three year-long dispute over the Viaduct Quay retail development has finally ended with Ports of Auckland paying out more than NZ$100,000 to disgruntled tenants.

Garden Goliath battles Robert on name: A greenlumbed Aucklander who just happens to have the surname of a New Zealand gardening legend is making a chain of national garden centres see red over his plans to expand his business.

TransAlta lifts profit on higher scales: TransAlta Corp's first quarter profit has been risen 11 percent, reflecting higher electricity sales and its increased investment in its New Zealand subsidiary.
THE PRESS
Good year for NZ shares: New Zealand shares have had nearly one year of double digit rolling annual returns, reports the Spicers investment group.

Skyline Ent lifts profit: Skyline Enterprises, the Queenstown-based investor in the Christchurch Casino and owner of the Queenstown and Rotorua gondolas, has lifted full-year profit 42.5 percent to $6.7 million from $4.7 million the previous year.

Timaru post: Brian Tierney, chief executive of the Port of Timaru, says he has advised the board he will retire from the post on June 30, not resign from it as reported in the business pages on Saturday.
